item.title: Fish Dam Road Hike — Mon Oct 26, 2:00 PM — Eno River State Park - Cabelands Access
item.description:
Join a Ranger to explore remnants of the historic trading path known as Fish Dam Road. We will hike about 4 miles in total, including at least a mile of off trail hiking along old roads. One major creek crossing and the ability to navigate some tricky terrain is required.
At least 1 mile of hiking is off trail with one major creek crossing and some hilly terrain. This hike can be difficult for those unfamiliar with off trail hiking. item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Tue Oct 27 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: The Battle of Shallow Ford: An Exhibition of Watercolors and Words — Tue Oct 27 — Welborn Gallery
item.description:
On Display September 3 – Octobe 30, 2026
This collection of “watercolors” by master craftsman Rick Jones is accompanied by storyboards of “words” by artist and writer, Marilyn Ingram. The story, unfolding during a time where there were no cameras, cell phones, or even a typewriter, is told through the eyes of artists, field correspondents who would paint, draw or write a journal. The paintings include scenes at the Shallow Ford and nearby battle area, Moravian settlements along the great wagon road, and annual commemoration in Huntsville, NC. The words are researched through works including “Records of the Moravians” and NC State Archives. This exhibition is presented in partnership with The Lewisville Area Arts Council and was supported by the America 250 NC Community Grant.
An opening reception will be held September 3 from 5-7pm at the Yadkin Cultural Arts Center.
Refreshments will be served.
Free Admission, all are welcome to attend.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Tue Oct 27, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

Hosted at the Shinleaf section of Falls Lake State Recreation Area located at 13708 New Light Road. Wake Forest NC 27587. Highly encouraged to bring a pair of binoculars and water bottle. item.description:

item.title: Duke Pluriversal Studio Inaugural Open House — Tue Oct 27, 5:00 PM — Rubenstein Arts Center
item.description:
Please join Pluriversal Studio and its supporters, including Deborah Rutter, Ranji Khanna, Jerome Lynch, Tracy Futhey, Leo Ching, and more on October 27th, 5-6pm at Rubenstein Arts Center, 2nd Floor as we share our vision for this new initiative at this inaugural open house.
Students of all levels and schools interested in the overlap of engineering, the arts, and humanities especially welcome!
Food and refreshments for all
Pluriversal Studio is an extension of the FHI Social Practice Lab & its Mellon supported Artistic Research Initiative. It is a collaborative effort between DukeArts, FHI, Trinity, Pratt, OIT, and Duke Libraries. We hope to bridge art, engineering and the humanities on our campus and beyond, bringing together students, faculty, and staff, as well exciting guests and collaborators through the creation of signature projects and public interventions.

item.title: AGS Phillips Family International Lecture with Gina Raimondo — Tue Oct 27, 5:30 PM — Page Auditorium
item.description:
Join AGS for the Fall 2026 Ambassador Dave and Kay Phillips Family International Lecture, featuring Gina Raimondo, Co-chair & CEO of RAISE US and 40th U.S. Secretary of Commerce.
Secretary Raimondo is currently Co-Chair & CEO of RAISE US, a national, nonpartisan organization partnering with states, employers, training partners, and workers to help Americans make a successful transition to an AI economy. She was the 75th governor of Rhode Island, and Chair of the Democratic Governors Association. She is a distinguished fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations.
As secretary of commerce, she focused on making America competitive, encouraging innovation and growth, and advancing economic and national security. Her portfolio included manufacturing, economic development, and AI safety and policy.
She holds a BA in economics from Harvard University and a PhD from Oxford University, and she is a graduate from Yale Law School.
This event is part of We the People: A Duke & Durham

item.title: NCLAFF. A POET — Tue Oct 27, 6:30 PM — None
item.description:
Un Poeta (A Poet). 2025 Dir. Simón Mesa Soto (Colombia). Span / Eng Sub. 120 min.
Oscar Restrepo's obsession with poetry has brought him no glory. Aging and erratic, he has succumbed to the cliché of the poet in the shadows. Meeting Yurlady, a teenage girl from humble roots, and helping her cultivate her talent brings some light to his days. But dragging her into the world of poets may not be the way. Winner of Un Certain Regard, Cannes Film Festival 2025.
Special poetry recital before the film. 6:30 pm.
FEATURING:
Leila Zak. First-place winner, Pulitzer Young Adult Contest, Human Rights category. 2026. Duke Junior
Natalia María Harnisch. A.R. Ammons Poetry Contest 1st Place Winner, Division V, 2026. Duke Senior.
Source: Duke Arts, Duke University

item.title: Duke Arts Presents: Christian McBride & Ursa Major — Tue Oct 27, 7:30 PM — Bryan Center Reynolds Industries Theater
item.description:
Eleven-time GRAMMY-winning bassist Christian McBride is one of the most influential figures in jazz today. A virtuoso performer, composer, and bandleader, prolific educator and advocate, and host of NPR's "Jazz Night in America," McBride is equally at home across genres from straight-ahead jazz to R&B, hip-hop, and classical music.
In Ursa Major, McBride is joined by four exciting rising stars, including saxophonist Nicole Glover, guitarist Ely Perlman, pianist Mike King, and drummer Savannah Harris. Together they bring a fresh, high-energy approach to the bandstand.
A celebrated mentor as well as performer, McBride created URSA Major to spotlight emerging voices while continuing the collaborative spirit at the heart of jazz.
Source: Duke University

item.title: History at High Noon: Maco Light — Wed Oct 28, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Speaker: Holli Saperstein, Executive Director, Wilmington Railroad Museum
Join us for a spooky edition of History at High Noon as we explore the mystery of the Maco Light, one of North Carolina’s most famous ghost stories! Reported for more than a century near old train tracks in Brunswick County, this legend tells the story of a ghostly railroad conductor named Joe Baldwin. After a tragic accident, believers have claimed to spot Baldwin’s spirit searching for his lost head. This talk will examine the real history behind the tale and how the story became an important part of local folklore, attracting visitors and curiosity from across the country!
For questions, please contact Stacey Smith at (919) 814-7032.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Teacher Discussion: Unpacking American Indian Heritage Month — Wed Oct 28, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Unpacking American Indian Heritage Month Wed. Oct. 28, 2026 | 6:00–7:00 pm (followed by Q&A)
A free virtual discussion for K-12 educators
American Indian Heritage Month each November offers a powerful chance for educators to highlight the rich cultures, histories, and ongoing contributions of American Indian communities in North Carolina. In preparation, K–12 educators are invited to join DNCR’s NC American Indian Heritage Commission to deepen essential understandings of contemporary American Indian tribes across the state while dispelling common misconceptions and stereotypes.
Participants will explore practical ideas, vetted resources, and culturally grounded approaches that support meaningful integration of Native people, stories, and perspectives into classroom instruction, during November and throughout the entire school year.
Educators in attendance can request a .1 CEU form after the event.
Don’t miss this opportunity to strengthen your practice and ensure your students

This historical fiction novel, based in 1951 North Carolina, has an intertwined loved story complicated by a case of polio and an overseas deployment. It is a rich story of male friendship, rivalry, and learning your place in the world.

item.title: Dr. M.T. Pope House Presents: Evelyn's Book Club — Wed Oct 28, 6:30 PM — Dr. M.T. Pope House Museum
item.description:
This program honors Evelyn Pope by reading books.
Evelyn, a college librarian born in 1908 and died in 1995, loved a variety of books from The Adventures of Tom Sawyer to Shakespeare and James Baldwin. The program brings community members together monthly at the museum to discuss books, focusing on works by Black writers or featuring Black subjects, including fiction and non-fiction. Discussions will use questions to facilitate conversation.
"Mama Day" by Gloria Naylor Wednesday, Feb. 25 "The Black Angels: The Untold Story of the Nurses Who Helped Cure Tuberculosis" by Maria Smilios Wednesday, April 22 "A Visitation of Spirits" by Randall Kenan Wednesday, June 24 "Becoming Lunsford Lane: The Lives of an American Aeneas" by Craig Friend Wednesday, Aug. 26 "Ring Shout" by P. Dejeli Clark Thursday, Oct. 29Registration opens Jan. 23. An optional book bundle will be available to purchase at registration. Books can be picked up at the Dr. M.T. Pope House Museum.
Source: NC Cultural

item.title: The Magician Screening & Live Score — Wed Oct 28, 7:00 PM — Carolina Theatre of Durham
item.description: The Carolina Theatre of Durham presents a screening of Rex Ingram’s 1926 silent horror film “The Magician” set to an original live score written by Stack / Pratt / Mislock: Andy Stack (Wye Oak), Kelly Pratt (Beirut) and Tim Mislock (“Hedwig and the Angry Inch”). The artists will perform the original live score for the first time ever inside the Carolina Theatre’s historic 1,000-seat Fletcher Hall on October 28. Based on the 1908 novel by Somerset Maugham, “The Magician” traces the life of sculptor Margaret Dauncey (Alice Terry), who is paralyzed when one of her statues falls on her. Surgeon Dr. Arthur Burdon (Iván Petrovich) guides Margaret to a miraculous recovery, one witnessed by an unsetting, occultist magician named Oliver Haddo (Paul Wegener). Whilst Arthur and Margaret fall in love and plan to marry, Haddo cunningly stalks the bride-to-be with evil intent, hoping to continue his nefarious experiments in pursuit of creating and restoring human life. item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Oct 29 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: The Battle of Shallow Ford: An Exhibition of Watercolors and Words — Thu Oct 29 — Welborn Gallery
item.description:
On Display September 3 – Octobe 30, 2026
This collection of “watercolors” by master craftsman Rick Jones is accompanied by storyboards of “words” by artist and writer, Marilyn Ingram. The story, unfolding during a time where there were no cameras, cell phones, or even a typewriter, is told through the eyes of artists, field correspondents who would paint, draw or write a journal. The paintings include scenes at the Shallow Ford and nearby battle area, Moravian settlements along the great wagon road, and annual commemoration in Huntsville, NC. The words are researched through works including “Records of the Moravians” and NC State Archives. This exhibition is presented in partnership with The Lewisville Area Arts Council and was supported by the America 250 NC Community Grant.
An opening reception will be held September 3 from 5-7pm at the Yadkin Cultural Arts Center.
Refreshments will be served.
Free Admission, all are welcome to attend.

item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.

item.title: NC Public Librarian Certification Commission — Fri Oct 30, 10:30 AM — DNCR
item.description:
The NC Public Librarian Certification Commission was formed in 1936 to set minimum standards for public librarians to protect and maintain public library resources, to assure professional management and administration of library services, to meet the personnel requirements for State Aid administered by the Library of NC, and to guarantee the best possible public library service to all North Carolinians.
The North Carolina General Statute 143B-68 states that the commission must be comprised of: the Chairman of the public libraries section of NCLA, two individuals named by the Governor upon nomination of the NCLA, the dean of a State or regionally accredited graduate school of librarianship in North Carolina appointed by the Governor, and one member at large appointed by the Governor. Commission members appointed by the Governor serve 4-year terms, all others serve 2-year terms.

item.title: Batty Bio Blitz — Sat Oct 31, 9:00 AM — Visitor Center
item.description:
Bats are often misunderstood because of their association with Halloween and all things spooky - from their leathery wings to their cave-like habitats. But these fascinating animals are far more than a symbol of the spooky season. Bats play an important role in our ecosystems and provide valuable benefits to the natural world. Come visit our Batty Bio Blitz display at the Visitor Center to discover more about bat ecology, their unique adaptations, the important roles they play in our ecosystems, and how we can help conserve and protect these remarkable animals. Registration is not required. For more information or questions, please email andra-claire.greene@ncparks.gov.

item.title: Death and Mourning in the Mountains: A Special Guided Tour at Vance Birthplace — Sat Oct 31, 10:00 AM — Governor Zebulon B. Vance Birthplace
item.description:
Join us at Vance Birthplace on Saturday, Oct. 31 for our new Death and Mourning in the Mountains tour to learn how the culture around death and funerary practices changed throughout the 1800s. Led by site staff, you’ll move through the historic grounds to explore how the Appalachian climate and cultures of Western North Carolina as well as technological advances in the funeral industry shaped the end of life in the mountains.
Tours are offered at 10am and 1pm and will last approximately 90 minutes, including an optional hike to the old Vance family cemetery. Tickets cost $10.70 per person via Zeffy. Spots are limited, so we recommend registering in advance. Join us to learn, ask questions, and connect with the region’s history through this rarely discussed chapter of Appalachian history.
If you have any questions, please feel free to reach out to us at vance@dncr.nc.gov or give us a call at (828) 645-6706!

House tours are given on-demand Thursdays through Saturdays from 10 AM to 3 PM. Tours are also available on Sundays from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM
Come learn about William Lenoir, a Captain during the American Revolution, who fought in the Battle of King's Mountain. You will also learn about his family, who inherited the house; the enslaved people who lived and worked on the plantation; and the site's history through the Civil War.
Tours last 45 minutes to an hour. Admission rates for tours are $7/adults and $5/children ages 14 and under
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Plant Dyes Demonstration — Sat Oct 31, 10:00 AM — President James K. Polk Historic Site
item.description:
Come out to the President Polk Site and chat with Amelia as she demos plant dye techniques. This is an interactive demo and visitors who would like to participate will have the opportunity to get hands on with the dyes!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Spooky Spiders on Rendezvous Mountain — Sat Oct 31, 10:00 AM — Rendezvous Mountain
item.description:
Join Rangers at the upper parking lot by the picnic tables and learn about common spiders we see around Rendezvous Mountain. We will take a short walk to look for spiders in their habitat, then come back to the tables and do a spider craft activity. Please call the park office to sign up. 336-667-5072
Source: NC Cultural Resources
